messages:
maria: heads-up: after the RBAC role split landed in staging, the gpu-job-controller pods are crashing on init with KMS decrypt failures (403). seen across both us-west and eu clusters.

maria: stacktrace in init logs: `error: failed to decrypt envelope: access denied (status=403)`

maria: rolling back is ok but wanted to surface since this looks like a permissions regression from the least-privilege changes we applied to the deploy SA.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-20T10:02:31Z rolled: ci/gpu-job-controller v2.7.1 -> v2.8.0 (maria/rbac-split) :warning:

toby: thanks for flagging. which SA is the controller using? gpu-job-controller uses `svc-gpu-controller@redwood-prod` with KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd.

maria: yep that's the one. quick grep shows the ClusterRoleBinding change removed `kms:Decrypt` annotation binding for that SA during the split.

elena: can you paste the ClusterRole/Role you applied? suspect we made the old aggregated role too narrow.

maria: pasted snippet:
```
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: infra-gpu-access
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]
# note: prior aggregated role also allowed kms:Decrypt via external webhook annotation
```

sanjay: hmm our KMS access is actually provided by a policy attached to the GKE Workload Identity mapping + an annotation on the ServiceAccount. If the RoleBinding moved to a namespaced Role w/o the annotation copy, the mapping won't apply.

jessica: audit-bot just ingested logs: `audit-bot: detected 37 failed cryptographic ops by svc-gpu-controller@redwood-prod between 10:03-10:05 UTC`

elena: priority: confirm whether the SA lost the `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account` annotation during the refactor. that's the common cause.

maria: checking now — looks like the refactor introduced a templating bug. the role/template that assigns the annotation uses `{{ .namespace }}` but the controller SA is in `kube-system` and template path expected `infra-*`. so annotation wasn't set during the patch.

toby: ok action plan: 1) hotpatch staging: reapply correct annotation and redeploy controller (maria). 2) add e2e check in the RBAC refactor PR verifying KMS decrypt success for the controller (sanjay/elena). 3) create follow-up ticket to add an audit rule that alerts on repeated KMS 403s for critical controller SAs (jessica).

maria: hotpatch applied to staging, restarted pods. logs now show KMS decrypt success and controller moved to Running. :thumbsup:

jessica: filed SEC-4873: "RBAC refactor: ensure workload-identity annotations preserved" with acceptance criteria + screenshot of logs. linking to PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rbac/pull/412

sanjay: will add an integration test that creates a fake KMS-encrypted secret and asserts the controller can decrypt it post-deploy. should catch template regressions.

elena: we should also update the release checklist to run a dry-run that verifies SA annotations for any refactor touching clusterroles/rolebindings.

maria: good catch everyone. we'll schedule a quick postmortem tomorrow to capture root cause and docs. tagging @sanjay to lead remediation.

toby: small note for follow-up: audit logs show similar 403 spikes 3 weeks ago but we didn't connect them to the RBAC change then. expanding the alert window to 30d might help.

audit-bot: created alert rule "KMS_403_spike_controller_sas" (severity=high) targeting svc-* controller SAs.

maria: closing this thread once we have the postmortem notes in SEC-4873. thanks all.
